playback: Unmodified CLI stdout/stderr; commands and pauses are paced for readability.

scenes.title: A rename deserves a decision.
scenes.subtitle: An existing nullable column disappears. Generation stops before writing SQL.
scenes.caption: The existing row is still there. No implicit DROP / ADD.

commands.stderr: symmetria: destructive migration requires explicit rename hints or allowDestructive (--allow-destructive)

scenes.title: Make the rename explicit.
scenes.subtitle: rename.json maps users.email to users.mail using physical SQL names.
scenes.caption: The migration renames the column and keeps Ada's email.

scenes.title: Saved SQL stays under review.
scenes.subtitle: An intentional removal is generated. Lint still checks its up.sql afterward.
scenes.caption: The snapshot already matches the code. Lint still exits 1 for the pending DROP.

commands.stdout:
DESTRUCTIVE 000003_remove_mail: Statement 1: Removes data or a database object.
            Review the exact SQL and deploy dependent application changes first.

scenes.title: Exercise the SQL on PostgreSQL.
scenes.subtitle: Verify creates disposable databases and tests installation, upgrade and rollback.
scenes.caption: Data hooks assert that an existing user survives up, down and reapplication.

commands.stdout:
Data check [up]: existing user retained.
Data check [down]: existing user retained.
Data check [reapply]: existing user retained.
Verified 2 migrations: installation, upgrade, rollback and reapplication.

scenes.title: Catch the smaller differences.
scenes.subtitle: A manual change removes a default without changing the column type.
scenes.caption: Drift checks defaults, identity, constraints, enums and index validity.

commands.stdout: ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN active DROP DEFAULT;

scenes.title: Adopt checks the live schema.
scenes.subtitle: History cannot be re-baselined while the database differs from the target.
scenes.caption: The failed adoption leaves the recorded migration history intact.

commands.stderr:
symmetria: schema does not match the adoption/recovery target
default-mismatch      "users"."active" (expected TRUE, found nothing)

scenes.title: Reconcile, then adopt.
scenes.subtitle: Restore the declared default and verify the baseline again.
scenes.caption: The live schema matches before migration history is recorded.

commands.stdout: ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN active SET DEFAULT TRUE;

scenes.title: See the commit boundary.
scenes.subtitle: Online index construction runs outside a transaction under a session-wide lock.
scenes.caption: The plan prints the exact SQL and its nontransactional execution mode.

commands.stdout:
-- group 1: none · 000002_email_index
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY "users_email_idx" ON "users" USING btree ("email");

scenes.title: A partial failure stays visible.
scenes.subtitle: Duplicate emails prevent the concurrent unique index from completing.
scenes.caption: SQLSTATE, statement number and durable incomplete state identify the recovery boundary.

commands.stderr:
symmetria: migration "000002_email_index" failed (up, statement 1, SQLSTATE 23505): could not create unique index "users_email_idx"

SQL:
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY "users_email_idx" ON "users" USING btree ("email")
could not create unique index "users_email_idx"

commands.stdout:
applied 000001_initial
incomplete 000002_email_index · up · 0 confirmed statements · repair required

scenes.title: Reconcile data. Verify the boundary.
scenes.subtitle: Keep the original user, remove the invalid index, then explicitly request a retry.
scenes.caption: Repair replays the historical target in a disposable database to check the starting schema.

commands.stdout:
Removed 1 duplicate row; retained the original user.
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY users_email_idx;

scenes.title: Retry the unchanged migration.
scenes.subtitle: The concurrent index completes and the live catalog matches the generated schema.
scenes.caption: One original user retained. A valid unique index. A clean migration journal.
